summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 96% YoY to INR446 crore and FY26 PAT rose 102% to INR111 crore; FY27 guided to 45-55% revenue growth.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR446 crore (+96% YoY), EBITDA of INR80 crore (+96%) and PAT of INR54 crore-equivalent growth of 120%, with FY26 revenue of INR1,026 crore (+94%), EBITDA of INR95 crore (8.1% margin) and PAT of INR111 crore (+102%). Order book was stated at about INR1,884 crore at March 2026, with management later citing about INR3,000 crore in hand as of the call date and a FY27 bid pipeline of about INR6,000 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 45-55%, EBITDA margin of 16-18% and PAT margin around 11%. Several answers were inconsistent on figures (order book scope, PAT margin, guidance ranges), and the reclassification of expenses across quarters drew repeated analyst questions.

segments.name: SRM standalone
segments.commentary: Order book about INR2,112 crore of the INR3,000 crore in hand per management; FY27 standalone revenue guided at INR1,150-1,300 crore. Road orders include Nashik Ring Road (14 km, INR483 crore, 12-month timeline, appointed date pending) and a NHAI Thalout landslide remedial work of INR128 crore.

segments.name: MIPL (Maccaferri Infrastructure, 51% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Order book above INR850 crore of the INR3,000 crore in hand; FY27 revenue guided at INR400-450 crore. Acquisition's final installment of INR19 crore is due in June 2026.

segments.name: Slope stabilisation
segments.commentary: Makes up about 51% of the order book per management; margins described as much better than road, with strike rate of 33-50% versus 5-7% in roads. Competitors named: Spar Geo, Bharat, Pioneer and KEC.

segments.name: Roads and bridges
segments.commentary: About 40-some percent of the order book; management says road tenders are highly competitive with a 5-7% strike rate and that it bids selectively for margins.

segments.name: Tunnels
segments.commentary: About 2% of the order book; management is waiting on Ladakh tunnel projects.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at approximately 45-55%, with EBITDA margin of 16-18% and PAT margin around 11%.
FY27 consolidated revenue guided at INR1,500-1,750 crore (SRM standalone INR1,150-1,300 crore plus MIPL INR400-450 crore); PAT margin guided at 8.75-10.25%.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR2,000 crore; bid pipeline about INR6,000 crore with expected conversion of 60-70%.
Order book expected to be around INR4,000 crore by end FY27 per management, and about INR6,000 crore including execution, with revenue around INR3,000 crore in three years.
FY27 capex estimated at about INR250 crore, to be funded mainly by equipment debt, with the rest from internal accruals.
Management said there is no plan for a QIP for the next three months.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex of about INR152 crore, of which INR130 crore was funded by new equipment debt.
FY27 capex estimated at about INR250 crore, mainly machinery purchases for new projects (Nashik Ring Road, Palghar in Maharashtra).
Company policy is project-specific equipment financing, repaid as the project completes.
Abu Dhabi branch office established in UAE; talks with about 4 clients in Oman (Muscat) and UAE (Fujairah), none confirmed; no international capex allocated yet.
Ministry guidance: MoRTH circulars on bitumen and diesel cover about 80-85% of price escalation.
demand_pricing: Order book in hand: management cited INR1,884 crore at March 2026 (standalone) and about INR3,000 crore as of the call date, after roughly INR1,500 crore of orders received in the quarter.
FY26 order inflow about INR1,097 crore; FY27 bid pipeline about INR6,000 crore, with about INR1,600 crore of bids submitted and awaiting results.
No HAM (hybrid annuity) project won to date; management said it is bidding for these.
Management reported no slowdown in bidding despite geopolitical concerns.
Order book size: slope projects typically INR30-180 crore, road projects are much larger; management expects roughly INR2,500-2,800 crore of the INR6,000 crore pipeline to materialise.

Gross margin concerns: analyst questioned Q4 gross margin of about 21% versus Q2/Q3 53-54%; management attributed it to unbilled revenue and inventory purchases entered in COGS and said full-year gross margin is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Why did COGS jump sharply in Q4 FY26, and are the high Q2/Q3 gross margins sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Aashni Mahajan said COGS rose in line with revenue and that about INR130 crore of unbilled revenue and INR47 crore of inventory purchases were booked in COGS in Q4; full-year gross margin is said to be stable. An analyst understood the full-year gross margin guidance as about 35%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book execution timeline, and what is the difference between INR1,800 crore and INR3,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said roads typically have two years to complete (Nashik Ring Road one year), slopes about one year (sometimes 1.5). The INR3,000 crore is order book in hand, all unexecuted, to be executed over about two years; the INR1,800 crore is the March 31 figure. INR6,000 crore pipeline conversion is expected at 60-70%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did long-term debt rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahajan said the increase is equipment financing: INR130 crore of the INR152 crore FY26 fixed-asset additions was debt-funded, for mobilisation on new and old projects. Management said debt is project-specific and is repaid when the project moves out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for debt and equity funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 capex of about INR250 crore will be funded by equipment debt, and the rest from internal accruals. CFO said debt could rise a little depending on market offers. Management said there is no QIP plan for the next three months and was open to dilution in future.

qa_highlights.question: Why were some Q4 orders not notified to the exchanges?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said slope orders are small (INR30-80 crore each), that about seven or eight such orders were not separately reported, and that MIPL's orders were not notified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the clarification on the reclassification of expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the change of auditor led to reclassification of wages and subcontractor costs between COGS and other expenses; FY26 numbers are restated on a consistent basis. Other expenses of INR68 crore for FY26 comprise INR48 crore operational and INR16 crore admin expenses (as stated).

risks_watch: Gross margin volatility: Q4 gross margin of about 21% vs 53-54% in Q2/Q3; reclassification of expenses across quarters makes quarterly comparisons less reliable.
Order book quoted inconsistently (INR1,800 crore March vs INR3,000 crore as of call vs INR4,000 crore by FY27 end), and guidance ranges were restated during the call (PAT margin, revenue).
Working capital: INR37 crore receivable from a project over a year old classified as non-current; INR76 crore contract assets expected to bill next quarter.
Debt rising with equipment financing; FY27 debt level unclear and debt-to-equity figure quoted as '0.3% to 0.2%' which appears to be a mis-statement.
Road-heavy growth may dilute margins; management says it bids selectively but road strike rate is only 5-7%.
No HAM project won yet; international expansion (Oman, UAE) not yet converted to orders.
Slow revenue visibility: the Nashik Ring Road appointed date has not yet been received.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth and pipeline, but evasive or inconsistent on several numbers (order book scope, PAT margin, debt-to-equity, and the reasons for COGS and expense reclassification), with frequent deferrals to the CFO and a promise to follow up offline.
key_quotes: I see no structural reasons for this momentum to slow.
We will be putting capex only for the purchase of the machinery and other will be raised from in-house only.
We will deliver whatever we promise.

adds.what: New machinery for Nashik Ring Road and Palghar projects (equipment, not plant capacity; capex ~INR250 cr FY27)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at 45-55% (consolidated INR1,500-1,750 cr), backed by INR3,000 cr order book as of call date and INR250 cr debt-funded machinery for Nashik Ring Road and Palghar; but guidance figures were internally inconsistent and the INR6,000 cr pipeline is only partly expected to convert (INR2,500-2,800 cr), so backing is partial.
